docs.text: StarMade Guides Welcome to the StarMade Guides! This is a replica of the in-game documentation built by the community to help players get started in StarMade. The old documentation can be found here , but is not maintained. For the most up to date information please refer to this site or to the in-game guides. Click on the Introduction to get started. Site Navigation Browse the navigation on the left to find guides on various topics. Topics are broken out into sections of general gameplay mechanics and you can search for keywords as needed in the top left searchbar. Downloading StarMade While the Steam version of Starmade costs money currently, the Demo version on Steam is identical to the official release. You can also download the game for free off of the official website . If you wish to support StarMade you may wish to consider supporting the development of the new StarMade Galaxy rewrite. Launcher Versions The newly created StarMade Launcher v4 has been released on Steam as well as the official downloads page . If you've had StarMade installed for some time please make sure to update to the new launcher to keep your game up to date; Steam will do this automatically. Within the new launcher you have the ability to manage multiple installed versions of StarMade, manage your mods, and other settings like java memory allocations. StarMade Accounts With the new v4 launcher you can manage multiple StarMade accounts right there in the app. You can also register accounts at the official StarMade account portal online. These accounts are important as they connect your in-game account across servers and can be integrated into the StarMade Discord to verify your in-game username. System Requirements Currently StarMade runs on Linux and Windows natively, however MacOS support is somewhat spotty at the time of writting. You can find all the minimum system requirements on the Steam page .

docs.text: StarMade Galaxy StarMade Galaxy is a new version of StarMade built in Unity SRP that one of the developers of the original game is working on in their free time. This version of the game is publicly unavailable, however you can support Schema via Patreon to gain access to the experimental branch of StarMade Galaxy, but there is currently no build yet . Note that this is completely optional, and that the official Java version is still maintained and widely used throughout the community. If you're new to StarMade the suggestion remains to stick to the Java version from Steam or the official StarMade site . There is a teaser trailer of StarMade Galaxy available on YouTube . Galaxy FAQ As you might expect the community has a lot of questions regarding how the two StarMades compare and what might one day be transferable. I've tried to compile the most commonly asked questions below and the answers from the developers. Please note, all of this is subject to change without notice and is just what we know so far as a community, not an actual plan for development. Please do not yell at our lovely developers due to any of these comments! What shape will planets take in StarMade Galaxy? "Cube planets with smoothed terrain edges" DukeofRealms What about all the work that's gone into round planets? "The round planets that was worked on is still coming in Java StarMade. Although, they were lots of plates, Derp can explain more on that." DukeofRealms What about all the good work the community has put into StarMade? "most features will be ported" VideoGoose Will StarMade Galaxy have dedicated servers? "Yes." DukeofRealms Will dedicated servers require GPUs? "No, it's not required" DukeofRealms "GPU will always be faster" Schema Will I be able to import ship blueprints? "I have some different systems planned, a lot of optimization, and some for just better utility and gameplay however, blueprints will be importable on a block basis - just don't expect your ship to work, lol" Schema How will star systems be structured now? "In the map, you see Regions (the cake slices + 1 middle) and Zones (in regions). Each zone will have a system that determines who controls it. This will be NPC or unowned. But I also plan to make each region matter for not only who's there, what's there, and other gameplay elements" Schema "Systems are still technically defined in a cube, but sectors are more or less not the deciding factor anymore" Schema Can I help make StarMade Galaxy? "I'll be open for it. Also for the mod team of course" Schema Will most of the non game infrastructure like the Discord and dock be carried over? "Yeah, we'll be also launching a fluxer instance. Because discord is getting wild" Schema So you jump to a system now and then fly inside of it? "yes, the only limiting factor would be that planets can't generate fast enough. They are a few hundreds of magnitude fasten than the old system, but still the planets you see in the video take ~3-5 sec to generate" Schema Will there be moons? "there are also moons, which I'll probably make round" Schema "they will not be bumpable like asteroids are and they will likely get gravity" Schema Will there be fauna and aliens? "ye" Schema Will we get water physics for planetary water? "planned" Schema Will we get cross entity lighting? "It's within possibility but not yet there, since it would cost a bit, but it's theoretically possible, yes. Also I'll do some dynamic lighting up close either way" Schema Why the rebase to Unity? "It's mostly because such deep cuts would have to be made to the old engine that it essentially would be a rewrite either way. I'm using the parts of unity that are actually good. Unity has a ton of problems, mostly the stuff they put upfront. All the good stuff is in the back" Schema

docs.text: Introduction to StarMade StarMade is a voxel-based space sandbox game. You explore a procedurally generated universe, build ships and stations block by block, gather resources, craft items, fight enemies, and team up with other players. The Universe at a Glance The universe is divided into Sectors and Systems . Pirates and other NPC Factions appear across the galaxy map. Planets and asteroids gather around stars, and asteroid belts vary in resources based on their distance from their star. Core Gameplay Loop Explore — fly through space, discover planets, asteroids, and trading stations Mine — collect raw ores and crystal shards from asteroids and planet surfaces Craft — refine materials into components and build blocks Build — construct and upgrade ships and stations Survive — defend yourself against pirates and rival players Game Modes Singleplayer You host your own universe. All admin commands are available. Blueprints are saved to the blueprints/ folder of your StarMade install. Multiplayer You connect to a shared server. Server rules govern admin commands and what you can build. Blueprints saved to a server are stored server-side. First Steps When you first spawn, you will be in astronaut mode — a floating humanoid character. The spawn location is configured by the server; by default it is sector 2, 2, 2 , home to a Trading Guild Trade Station where you can buy basic supplies. Your immediate goals: Get comfortable with character movement Familiarise yourself with the HUD Learn basic controls Find some asteroids and mine your first resources Tip: Check the navigation panel ( N by default) to locate nearby trading stations, asteroids, and planets from your starting position.

docs.text: HUD & Interface The HUD (Heads-Up Display) gives you live information about your character and ship at a glance. Astronaut HUD On foot you see: Crosshair in the centre of the screen. Hotbar at the bottom, with your health bar (green) just above it. Radar in the top-right corner, with your current sector coordinates below it. Use these when setting navigation waypoints. Target panel in the top-left corner while you have something selected ( F selects what you are looking at). On a planet, a location readout under the radar adds your position on the planet, altitude, biome, time of day and the current weather. Ship HUD When you fly a ship, bars curve around the crosshair: Side Bar What it shows Left Shield (yellow) Shield charge Left Armor / Structure Armor HP and structure HP Right Power (blue) Reactor power: what you have against what your systems are drawing Right Speed (white) Current speed Right Heat Heat from cannon and beam fire. Heat Sink blocks soak it up; once they are full, those weapons can't fire until it cools. Buffs (green) and debuffs (red) from weapon effects show up near the centre of the screen. A flash on the crosshair tells you what you hit: blue for shields, white for blocks, red for a character. Hotbar Ten slots mapped to keys 1–9 and 0 . The mouse wheel cycles slots (except in advanced build mode). On a slot with several block shapes, the wheel steps through those first. Holds: Items and blocks (astronaut mode) Weapons and systems (ship flight mode) Blocks to place (build mode) Panels & Menus Panel Default Key Description Inventory I Personal inventory and personal crafting Guides F8 These guides Shop B Buy and sell, when you are near a shop Navigation N Nearby objects, filters, and waypoints Galaxy Map M Star systems, territory and routes Catalog U Saved blueprints Faction H Faction management Fleets K Fleet management Reactor Insert (in a ship with a reactor) Reactors, chambers and stability Weapons G (in ship) Weapon groups and hotbar assignment Structure Delete (in ship) Ship systems, docked entities AI ; (in ship) AI settings for the ship Chat Enter Chat channels: general, your faction, and any you create or join. Pick PRIVATE MESSAGE on a channel member to start a private chat. Player List F1 (hold) Server info and online players Press F2 to free the mouse cursor without opening a panel. All keys can be changed in the options. Control Helpers Hints for the controls you can use right now appear on screen and change with what you are doing (on foot, flying, or building). Press / (default) to show or hide the full help screen.

docs.text: Character Movement Your character moves in two very different ways: walking where there is gravity , and floating freely in zero gravity . Gravity Planets always have gravity. On ships and stations you need a Gravity Unit block: look at it and press R to step into its gravity field. Its gravity pulls toward the bottom of the block, so place it the way you want "down" to point. Action Key Walk W A S D Sprint Double-tap W and hold Jump Space Crouch Left Shift (hold) Prone Z (press again or Space to stand) Look Mouse Activate a block R Crouching halves your speed and lowers your view. You stay crouched while there's a low ceiling above you. Prone is very slow but keeps you low to the ground. You can't go prone while swimming, sitting or climbing. Sprint only works going forwards. A Gravity Exit Unit used the same way takes you out of the field again. See Logic Basics . Ladders { "height": 240, "blocks": [ { "from": [0,0,0], "to": [4,0,4], "block": "GREY_HULL" }, { "from": [0,1,0], "to": [4,4,0], "block": "GREY_HULL" }, { "from": [0,4,-3], "to": [4,4,-1], "block": "GREY_HULL" }, { "from": [2,1,1], "to": [2,4,1], "block": "LADDER", "orient": 15 } ] } Walk into a Ladder block to grab it. Hold W to climb; let go and you slide back down. Press Space , S , A or D to let go of the ladder. Swimming In water you swim in the direction you look. Space swims up, and at the surface it climbs you out. You can't sprint or go prone in water. Zero Gravity Outside a gravity field you float freely in all six directions. Action Key Move forward / backward W / S Strafe left / right A / D Move up / down E / Q Slow drift Left Shift (hold) Look Mouse Align to the structure in front of you Space A Thrust Pack worn in your back slot makes you much faster in zero gravity. Aligning to a Structure When you are floating near a ship or station, press Space to align to it. You then move with the structure wherever it goes. This is very useful for: Boarding a moving ship through a hatch Working on the outside of a ship without drifting away Not being left behind when a crewed ship accelerates To let go, press Space again while not looking at the structure. If it is moving fast, the game asks you to confirm first. Magnetic Boots Magnetic Boots , worn in your feet slot, let you stand on any surface: ships, stations and planets, including walls, ceilings and cliff faces, with no gravity module needed. Press ` while looking at a surface within reach to stand on it. Press it at another surface to move onto that one. Press it while looking at nothing to let go. In zero gravity, Space (Align) also locks the boots on. To wear gear, drag it into its slot on the Equipment tab of your inventory. Tips In build mode, movement is the same as zero gravity, but you pass through blocks. Hold Left Shift to move much faster around large ships. Mining is done with a ship's salvage beam, not by hand. See Resources & Mining .

docs.text: Advanced Building Build mode has a radial menu of shape tools for placing blocks in geometric patterns, and an advanced build mode panel full of power tools. Together they dramatically speed up construction of large ships and stations. Advanced Build Mode You must be in Build Mode (inside a ship core or build block). Hold Left Ctrl to enter advanced build mode; the tool panel appears on the right side of the screen. Tap Left Ctrl twice to make it stick, and tap it again to leave. In advanced build mode: You aim with the mouse cursor instead of the centre of the screen. The mouse wheel rotates the selected block. The build size sliders apply, so one click can place or remove a whole area of blocks. The middle mouse button puts the block you are pointing at on your hotbar. Speed tip: Hold Left Shift in build mode to move much faster — essential for working on large structures. Build Tools Radial Menu Press the backtick key ( ` ) in Build Mode to open the radial menu of eight shape tools. Pick one from the ring, then click in the world to use it. How clicks work for every shape tool: Normally each click lands on a point 5 blocks in front of your camera , so you can build out into empty space. Hold Left Ctrl to click exactly on the block face under your cursor instead. Left-click starts a shape that places blocks; right-click starts one that removes them. The first click decides which. Removing needs you to click on actual blocks. A live preview shows the shape: yellow to place, red to remove. Press Escape to cancel a shape you have started. A finished shape is one undo step ( Ctrl+Z ). Shapes use your symmetry planes, remove filter and build size, and you need enough blocks in your inventory. The centre button of the radial menu toggles Hollow Mode : Box, Circle, Cylinder, Ellipsoid and Polygon are then built as empty shells or outlines instead of solid fills. Single The default mode. Place or remove one block (or one build-size area) per click. Line Draw a straight line of blocks. Click to set the start point . Click again to set the end point . The line is placed. Left Ctrl + mouse wheel cycles axis restriction: Auto, XY plane, XZ plane, YZ plane. Hold Left Shift to snap to straight lines and 45° diagonals. Box Fill a rectangular volume with blocks. Click to set the first corner . Click to set the opposite corner . The box is placed. Hollow mode builds only the six walls. Curve Draw a smooth curve. Click to set the start point . Click to set the end point . Click to set the control point . The curve bends toward it (it doesn't pass through it). Left Ctrl + mouse wheel cycles axis restriction. Hold Left Shift to snap angles. Circle Place a flat circle of blocks. Click to set the center . Click to set the radius . Left Ctrl + mouse wheel cycles the plane: Auto (facing you), XY, XZ, YZ. Hold Left Shift to snap the radius to 90° steps. Hollow mode builds a ring instead of a disc. Cylinder Build a cylinder. Click to set the base center . Click to set the radius . Click to set the height . While setting the radius, Left Ctrl + mouse wheel cycles the plane and Left Shift snaps it. Hollow mode builds an open tube with no ends. Ellipsoid Build a sphere or egg shape that fits inside a box. Click to set the first corner of the box. Click to set the opposite corner . The ellipsoid is placed. Hollow mode builds a shell one block thick. Polygon Build a flat shape with 3 to 8 corners. Before you start, Left Ctrl + mouse wheel sets how many corners it has (3 by default). Click to place each corner. The shape is placed as soon as you place the last one. Hollow mode builds only the outline. The axis, plane and corner settings reset to their defaults after each shape. Tool Panel General Orientation: shows which way the selected block will face. Click it to pick a shape; the mouse wheel rotates the block. Undo / Redo: also Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y . Build Size Three sliders (X, Y, Z) grow the area you place or remove with a single click. Scroll on a number to change it; right-click to reset it. The server sets the maximum ( PLAYER_MAX_BUILD_AREA in server.cfg , 100 by default). Symmetry Click XY , XZ or YZ , then click a block to put a symmetry plane there. Placing or removing a block on one side does the same on the other side. Use all three planes to build in eight places at once. Unset removes a plane. ODD puts the plane through the middle of a block instead of between blocks — use it for ships with an odd width. Mirror cubic blocks / Mirror non-cubic blocks (both on by default) turn blocks on the other side so they mirror the ones you place, for example wedges and weapon outputs facing outward on both sides. Selection Copy Brush: click *PICK AREA* , then click the two corners of the area to copy. Cut Mode: with this on, copying an area also removes those blocks and puts them in your inventory, like a cut. Undo puts them back. Paste: shows the copy as a preview; click to place it. You need the blocks in your inventory. While pasting: Mouse wheel rotates the copy (hold Left Shift for the X axis, Left Ctrl for the Z axis). Left Alt + arrow keys / Page Up / Page Down nudge it one block (add Left Shift for 10). Links between blocks (C/V) are kept when both ends are inside the copied area. Templates: save a copy under a name with tags, and load it later in any build. Search by name or tag. Remove/Replace: pick a block type (from the list or Pick with camera ). Right-click then only removes that type of block. Tick Only replace to swap those blocks for your selected block instead. This is invaluable for refitting ships . Highlight Selected in Entity: shows every block of the chosen type in the structure. Hotbar Save your hotbar as a named layout and load it again later. Color Finder Find a block by color: enter a hex color, pick a random one, or adjust saturation and brightness, then COPY TO HOTBAR . Block Mixer Choose up to 10 blocks. With the mixer on, each block you place is picked at random from them — great for weathered or patterned hulls. SET FROM HOTBAR fills it from your hotbar. Fill Tool Click Place Fill Origin and click a spot, then press Fill to flood the connected space (or the connected blocks of one type) with your selected block. The slider sets how many blocks each press adds. Build Helpers Shows a guide shape in the world ( line , circle , ellipsoid or torus ) to build along. Tick Restrict Building to Helper to only place blocks inside it. Docking Create Docking builds a new docked entity in two clicks: pick the rail, then pick where its core goes and which way it faces. See Docking & Turrets . Display Toggles that help while building: Buildlight: a flashlight for building in dark areas (also P ). Lighten up blocks: removes shadows so dark interiors are fully lit. Turn it off now and then to see how your ship really looks. Structure info, extra block info, reactor convex hull, and center of mass indicators.

docs.text: Power Basics A ship core makes no power of its own. Without a reactor your thrusters run at only 5% of their strength and weapons, shields and other systems don't work, so every real ship needs a reactor . This page covers the basics. See Reactors and Chambers for the details. Reactors and Stabilizers Reactor Power blocks make power. All reactor blocks that touch each other form one reactor , and the more blocks it has, the more power it makes. There is no special shape: any group works. A ship can have several reactors, but only one is active at a time. Inactive reactors make no power. You can switch the active reactor in the reactor menu (10 second cooldown). Reactor Stabilizer blocks keep the active reactor stable: The first 10 reactor blocks are free. After that you need one stabilizer per reactor block for 100% stability. Stabilizers can go anywhere on the ship , in as many groups as you like, at any distance from the reactor. Only your 20 biggest groups count. Below 100% stability your reactor still makes full power, but the ship takes extra damage from beams and explosions, up to 21× at 0%. { "height": 260, "blocks": [ { "from": [0,0,0], "to": [2,1,2], "block": "REACTOR_POWER" } ], "steps": [ { "text": "18 Reactor Power blocks touching each other form one reactor.", "blocks": [] }, { "text": "A separate group is a second reactor. Only one reactor is active at a time; switch between them in the reactor menu.", "blocks": [ { "from": [6,0,0], "to": [6,0,1], "block": "REACTOR_POWER" } ] }, { "text": "The first 10 reactor blocks are free, so 18 blocks need 8 stabilizers. They can be split into groups anywhere on the ship.", "blocks": [ { "from": [0,0,6], "to": [3,0,6], "block": "REACTOR_STABILIZER" }, { "from": [-4,0,0], "to": [-4,0,3], "block": "REACTOR_STABILIZER" } ] }, { "text": "A Reactor Conduit connects the reactor to a chamber.", "blocks": [ { "from": [1,2,1], "to": [1,3,1], "block": "REACTOR_CONDUIT", "orient": 2 }, { "from": [1,4,1], "to": [2,4,1], "block": "MOBILITY_CHAMBER" } ] } ] } Reactor Level A reactor's level goes up by one for every 150 reactor blocks (0–149 blocks is level 0). The level sets how big your chambers must be: at level 0 a single chamber block is enough, and each level after that needs about 7–8 more chamber blocks per chamber. Reactor Menu Open the Reactor Menu with Insert , from the radial menu ( Tab ), or with the REACTOR button on the top bar while you are in a ship with a reactor. It shows everything about your reactors: size, level, power, stability and capacity. Use its previous/next buttons to switch the active reactor, and open the chamber tree from it. Chambers and Reactor Capacity Reactor Chambers give your ship special bonuses and abilities. Connect them to the reactor (or to each other) with Reactor Conduit blocks. Each chamber uses some Reactor Capacity (RC), and you can't go over 100%. To set up a chamber, open the reactor menu, select the unspecified chamber, press Specify Chamber , and pick an option. You can then upgrade it for a stronger effect at the cost of more RC. There are eight chamber types: Chamber What it does Defence Shield capacity, armor HP and damage-type armor FTL Jump drive (distance, autocharge), jump inhibitors, warp gates Logistics Mining bonus, faster and cheaper factories, smaller cargo volume Mass Gravity fields Mobility Top speed, turn rate, thrust blast, anti-gravity Power Reactor boost and failsafe Recon Scanners: ores, cargo, cloaked ships Stealth Cloaking, jamming, anti lock-on See Chambers for each tree.

docs.text: Docking & Turrets StarMade uses a rail-based docking system . A ship docks to rail blocks on a station or another ship with a Rail Docker block. Rails handle fixed docking, turrets, moving platforms and elevators, cargo transfer, and automatic hangar docking. Rail Blocks Block Role Rail Docker Goes on the ship being docked; the connector end Rail Basic Standard rail on the host. Docked ships move along it in the direction of its arrow Rail Turret Axis Lets the docked entity rotate around one axis; chain two for a full turret Rail Rotator Clock Wise / Counter Clock Wise Turns a docked entity as it passes over Rail Mass Enhancer Raises how much docked mass the host can move at full speed Rail Speed Controller Sets how fast rails and rotators move Rail Load / Rail Unload Moves items between a docked ship's storage and the host's Pickup Point Docks ships automatically when they come close Pickup Rail A rail meant to sit next to a Pickup Point Shootout Rail Undocks anything that moves onto it, launching it at 5× rail speed Docking a Ship Place a Rail Docker on your ship. Each Rail Docker shows up as a Rail Docker entry in your Weapons panel. Put it on your hotbar. Fly within 100 m of a rail on the host, aim at the rail and fire with that slot selected. You don't have to line anything up: the docker's arrow face snaps onto the rail's arrow face like a magnet, and your ship ends up one block out from the rail. Only ships can dock (not stations), and the host must be neutral, your faction, public, or a faction you are in. After a dock attempt or undocking there is a 5 second cooldown. Create Docking in the advanced build mode panel builds a new docked entity right on a rail. See Advanced Building . Undocking Once docked, the Rail Docker entry on your hotbar is replaced by Undock . Fire with it selected to undock. You can also undock from the host: The Docks section of the structure panel has Undock All , Turrets and Normal buttons. Sending a logic signal to a docked ship's Rail Docker undocks it. A Shootout Rail at the end of a track launches ships off it. Mass Limits There is no hard size or mass limit for docking. Instead, each structure can move 50 mass of docked entities at full speed, plus 50 for every Rail Mass Enhancer on it. Enhancers can go anywhere on the host; they don't need linking, but each uses some reactor power. For every unit of mass over that limit, rails, rotators and AI turret turning slow down by 5%, to a minimum of 5% speed. Turrets A turret is built from docked entities on Rail Turret Axis blocks. One axis only rotates around one axis, so a full turret uses two: { "height": 300, "blocks": [ { "from": [-3,0,-3], "to": [3,0,3], "block": "GREY_HULL" } ], "steps": [ { "text": "Place a Rail Turret Axis on the host ship, arrow face up.", "blocks": [ { "at": [0,1,0], "block": "RAIL_TURRET_AXIS", "orient": 12 } ] }, { "text": "Dock the turret base to it with a Rail Docker facing down. The base turns left and right (yaw).", "blocks": [ { "at": [0,2,0], "block": "RAIL_DOCKER", "orient": 8 }, { "from": [-1,3,-1], "to": [1,4,1], "block": "DARK_GREY_HULL" } ] }, { "text": "Put a second Rail Turret Axis on the side of the base, and dock the barrel to it with a docker facing sideways. The barrel tilts up and down (pitch).", "blocks": [ { "at": [2,4,0], "block": "RAIL_TURRET_AXIS", "orient": 20 }, { "at": [3,4,0], "block": "RAIL_DOCKER", "orient": 16 }, { "from": [4,4,-1], "to": [4,4,1], "block": "DARK_GREY_HULL" }, { "from": [4,4,-5], "to": [4,4,-2], "block": "CANNON_BARREL" } ] }, { "text": "On the back of the barrel: a Cannon Computer linked to the barrels, a BOBBY AI Module so the turret aims by itself, and a Faction Module.", "blocks": [ { "at": [4,4,1], "block": "CANNON_COMPUTER" }, { "from": [4,4,-5], "to": [4,4,-2], "block": "CANNON_BARREL", "controller": [4,4,1] }, { "at": [4,4,2], "block": "BOBBY_AI_MODULE" }, { "at": [4,4,3], "block": "FACTION_MODULE" } ] } ] } A docker facing up or down on its entity turns around the vertical axis (yaw); a docker facing sideways tilts (pitch). The turret pivots on the docker, not the ship core, so the core can go anywhere on the turret. The barrel (the last entity in the chain) does the aiming and turns the base with it. Turrets can't rotate into blocks around them, so leave them room to turn. Heavier turrets turn slower under AI control. Turret AI Put a BOBBY AI Module on the barrel (the entity on the last axis) and tick Active ; it is set to the Turret type automatically. Turrets use the host's faction, so they don't need a Faction Module. From the host, , turns docked AI on and off and . resets turret rotation. See Ship & Turret AI for targeting, remote control and the rest of the AI settings. Shared Power and Shields Docked entities run on the reactor of the root ship , so turrets don't need their own reactor. While the host's shields are above 25%, they also take hits aimed at its docked entities. Automatic Docking (Pickup Points) For carrier hangars, place a Pickup Point next to a rail (usually a Pickup Rail ): An unpiloted ship whose Rail Docker comes within 3 m of an active Pickup Point docks to the rail next to it. Your own ship does too while you fly it. The Pickup Point can be turned on and off with logic. A docked ship remembers the Pickup Point it used. The Carrier Recall fleet order sends fleet ships back to their pickup points on the flagship. Moving Rails Ships docked to a Rail Basic move along the track by themselves, in the direction of the rail arrows, until the track ends. Use this for elevators, launch tubes and sliding doors. Rail Rotator Clock Wise / Counter Clock Wise : with nothing linked, it turns the docked entity 90° as it arrives. Link Activation Modules to it to set the angle: each active one adds 45°, and 9 or more make it turn non-stop. Link a Display Module with a number (0–360) to set an exact angle. Rail Speed Controller : link it to rails and rotators ( C / V ; Shift+V adds all touching rails), then link Activation Modules to it. Speed is the share of those modules that are on: 5 on and 5 off means 50% speed, and all off stops the track. Rails without a controller run at 50%. Cargo Rails Link the ship's Rail Docker to Storage blocks on the ship, and link a Rail Load or Rail Unload to Storage on the host: Rail Load moves items from the host's storage into the docked ship's storage. Rail Unload moves items from the docked ship to the host. Storage filters still apply.

Docked ships move along it in the direction of its arrow Rail Turret Axis Lets the docked entity rotate around one axis; chain two for a full turret Rail Rotator Clock Wise / Counter Clock Wise Turns a docked entity as it passes over Rail Mass Enhancer Raises how much docked mass the host can move at full speed Rail Speed Controller Sets how fast rails and rotators move Rail Load / Rail Unload Moves items between a docked ship's storage and the host's Pickup Point Docks ships automatically when they come close Pickup Rail A rail meant to sit next to a Pickup Point Shootout Rail Undocks anything that moves onto it, launching it at 5× rail speed
docs.title: Rail Blocks

docs.text: Place a Rail Docker on your ship. Each Rail Docker shows up as a Rail Docker entry in your Weapons panel. Put it on your hotbar. Fly within 100 m of a rail on the host, aim at the rail and fire with that slot selected. You don't have to line anything up: the docker's arrow face snaps onto the rail's arrow face like a magnet, and your ship ends up one block out from the rail. Only ships can dock (not stations), and the host must be neutral, your faction, public, or a faction you are in. After a dock attempt or undocking there is a 5 second cooldown. Create Docking in the advanced build mode panel builds a new docked entity right on a rail. See Advanced Building .
docs.title: Docking a Ship

docs.text: Once docked, the Rail Docker entry on your hotbar is replaced by Undock . Fire with it selected to undock. You can also undock from the host: The Docks section of the structure panel has Undock All , Turrets and Normal buttons. Sending a logic signal to a docked ship's Rail Docker undocks it. A Shootout Rail at the end of a track launches ships off it.
docs.title: Undocking

docs.text: There is no hard size or mass limit for docking. Instead, each structure can move 50 mass of docked entities at full speed, plus 50 for every Rail Mass Enhancer on it. Enhancers can go anywhere on the host; they don't need linking, but each uses some reactor power. For every unit of mass over that limit, rails, rotators and AI turret turning slow down by 5%, to a minimum of 5% speed.

docs.text: Put a BOBBY AI Module on the barrel (the entity on the last axis) and tick Active ; it is set to the Turret type automatically. Turrets use the host's faction, so they don't need a Faction Module. From the host, , turns docked AI on and off and . resets turret rotation. See Ship & Turret AI for targeting, remote control and the rest of the AI settings.

docs.text: Docked entities run on the reactor of the root ship , so turrets don't need their own reactor. While the host's shields are above 25%, they also take hits aimed at its docked entities.

docs.text: For carrier hangars, place a Pickup Point next to a rail (usually a Pickup Rail ): An unpiloted ship whose Rail Docker comes within 3 m of an active Pickup Point docks to the rail next to it. Your own ship does too while you fly it. The Pickup Point can be turned on and off with logic. A docked ship remembers the Pickup Point it used. The Carrier Recall fleet order sends fleet ships back to their pickup points on the flagship.
docs.title: Automatic Docking (Pickup Points)

docs.text: Ships docked to a Rail Basic move along the track by themselves, in the direction of the rail arrows, until the track ends. Use this for elevators, launch tubes and sliding doors. Rail Rotator Clock Wise / Counter Clock Wise : with nothing linked, it turns the docked entity 90° as it arrives. Link Activation Modules to it to set the angle: each active one adds 45°, and 9 or more make it turn non-stop. Link a Display Module with a number (0–360) to set an exact angle. Rail Speed Controller : link it to rails and rotators ( C / V ; Shift+V adds all touching rails), then link Activation Modules to it. Speed is the share of those modules that are on: 5 on and 5 off means 50% speed, and all off stops the track. Rails without a controller run at 50%.
docs.title: Moving Rails

docs.text: Link the ship's Rail Docker to Storage blocks on the ship, and link a Rail Load or Rail Unload to Storage on the host: Rail Load moves items from the host's storage into the docked ship's storage. Rail Unload moves items from the docked ship to the host. Storage filters still apply.

docs.text: Shipyards Shipyards are Space Station based systems that allow players to design ships in a temporary virtual creative environment and mass produce those designs from a loaded design, which is similar to a blueprint . You can also dock an existing ship into a shipyard to completely deconstruct it, or repair it using an existing loaded design. Construction Shipyards are constructed from a Shipyard Computer, Shipyard Modules, and a Shipyard Core Anchor. The computer, as with any other system computer , must have all of the Shipyard Modules slaved to it, as well as the Shipyard Core Anchor. A shipyard is only valid if the Shipyard Modules form a C shape, with both "ends" of the C being straight across from each other. A player can build as many or as few C-shaped sections as they want without affecting the function of a shipyard, provided that they are lined up. It should look something like this . The Shipyard Core Anchor can be placed anywhere within the perimeter of a Shipyard, but it is important that there are no solid blocks near it and that it is sufficiently spaced from the edges of the Shipyard to allow space for ships to take up. Note that wherever you place the Shipyard Core Anchor is where the actual Ship Core will appear. Ship designs will fail to load into the Shipyard Computer if there is not enough space inside the Shipyard Modules area for the ship. Ship Designs Shipyards use a special type of item called 'Designs' to function. They are similar to blueprints, and can be interchanged with blueprints through the Shipyard Computer. To create a new ship, use the Create New Design function in the Shipyard Computer. This will create a blank design with a virtual Ship Core at the position of the Shipyard Core Anchor. Blocks cannot be placed on the virtual ship except in build mode. The virtual ship is almost identical in function to a normal ship, except for a few important aspects: - The virtual ship cannot be edited except in the Shipyard's build mode. - The virtual ship cannot be undocked (however, use of Flight Mode without undocking is permitted, e.g. to test logic ) - The virtual ship has a hologram-styled shader applied to all of its blocks outside of the Shipyard's build mode. - When editing the virtual ship, regardless of permissions, the player uses a Creative Mode inventory. - Using blocks from a linked cargo in your inventory will not actually consume materials, rather behaving like creative mode. Test Sector The Test Sector is a virtual space in which a Design can be tested. Although it would seem to be a special Sector , it is not. It takes its surroundings from a specific location in System 0,0,0. As such, if there is a Pirate Station near that specific sector, it can cause problems when testing designs. Nominally, there would be no Pirate Stations present, and the player would be able to spawn in enemies of their choosing to fight or spawn static armored/shielded targets to test weapons on their design. It should be noted that, although it is assured that use of the Test Sector imparts no penalty on the player, death while in the Test Sector results in respawning at the player's most recently-activated Undeathinator. This can be problematic for some players who forgot to set their spawn point at their far-out base. Mass Production Assuming that all the necessary materials to construct a loaded ship design is present in the Shipyard Computer's inventory (which can be expanded with the use of Cargo), ships can be constructed, undocked, and reconstructed quickly. The Shipyard will, regardless of size, place up to 2,500 blocks per tick, meaning that a ship would have to be massive to take more than a couple minutes to be fully constructed with enough materials. Most small ships, such as drones, take only a few seconds to be constructed. In the Shipyard Computer, there is an option to undock the newly-constructed ship, so that all you have to do is move the new ship out of the way before re-loading and constructing the design again. When used properly, Shipyards can produce entire fleets of AI-controlled ships rapidly. Repairing Ships Shipyards can also be used to repair damaged ships or update mass-produced ships to a new standard design. This is done through a function of the Shipyard Computer, which basically deconstructs the ship and reconstructs it according to the loaded design. This design does not have to bear any resemblance to the original ship. Note that, since repairing completely deconstructs the ship and rebuilds it, it resets any saved hotbar configurations. A less destructive Ship repairing solution would be to use an Atrotech Beam instead. Deconstructing Ships Ships can dock to a Shipyard Core Anchor as they would with any other Rail , but with one notable difference; They must (counter-intuitively) have a Rail Docker somewhere on the ship. The position of the Rail Docker does not influence where the ship actually docks to the Core Anchor though. Instead, the ship is docked with the Ship Core at the position of the Shipyard Core Anchor. The Ship Core is always docked in alignment to the Shipyard Core Anchor. The Shipyard Computer can be used to deconstruct a docked ship and save it to a design, or simply deconstruct it without saving any design. This can be used to rapidly disassemble unused AI fleets or drones.

docs.text: Ship Basics A ship is the primary way to travel through space, fight enemies, and carry cargo. Every ship is built around a Ship Core block — the single block that defines the ship. Entering and Exiting a Ship Action Key Enter a ship (look at core) R Exit a ship (look away from ship) R When you enter a ship you are placed directly into its Ship Core . From there you can switch between the two ship modes. Ship Modes Press Z to toggle between flight mode and build mode while inside a ship. Ship Status Bars Every ship has three resource bars visible in the HUD: Bar Colour Description Hull / HP Red Total hull health. Reaches zero → ship destroyed Shield Blue Absorbs incoming damage before hull is hit Power Green Energy available for weapons, thrusters, and shields Hull and Armour Blocks making up the ship's hull each have individual hit points. The total ship HP is the sum of all block HP. Hull blocks provide high HP per block. Armour blocks reduce damage from each incoming hit before it is applied to HP — they act as a damage multiplier reduction. Weapons, computers, and other functional blocks are more fragile than hull/armour. A good ship design protects critical systems (reactors, computers, the core) with layers of hull and armour blocks. Rebooting If your power runs completely out while under attack, the ship enters a reboot state. Systems come offline temporarily. Keeping spare power capacity or using shields to buy time prevents this. docs.text: Building a Ship Ships are built block by block in Build Mode . This guide takes you through spawning your first ship and making it flight-ready. Spawning a Ship Core Press X (default: Spawn Ship) to place a new Ship Core block in the world. Give your ship a name when prompted. The core must have enough clear space around it to materialise. Tip: Don't look at the ground or a wall when spawning — the core needs room in the direction you are facing. After spawning, enter the ship with R (look at the core first), then switch to build mode with Z . Build Mode Basics In build mode you pass through all blocks and float freely. This makes it easy to work inside and around your ship. Action Key Place block Left Mouse Button Remove block Right Mouse Button Select block 1 – 9 , 0 / Mouse wheel Fast movement Left Shift (hold) Advanced Build Mode Left Ctrl (hold) Build tools radial menu ` Undo Ctrl+Z The selected block type is shown in your hotbar. Open your inventory ( I ) to move blocks into the hotbar slots. Making a Ship Flyable A bare ship core cannot move or fire weapons. At minimum you need: Power Reactor Module — place one or more anywhere on the ship. More reactor blocks = more power generation. The layout of reactor groups affects efficiency (see Ship Systems ). Thruster Module — place one or more anywhere on the ship. More thruster blocks = more top speed and acceleration. The direction the thrusters face doesn't matter mechanically — they push the ship forward in whatever direction the core is pointed. With both placed, switch to flight mode ( Z ) — you can now fly. Adding Weapons To arm your ship: Place a Weapon Computer block (e.g. Cannon Computer). Place several Weapon Barrel/Module blocks near it. These are the actual gun barrels. Open the Weapon Panel ( G ). Drag the weapon computer into a hotbar slot at the bottom of the panel. Close the panel and select that slot with the number keys. The weapon computer turns orange and pulses when it is the last selected/placed computer — this indicates it is "active" for connections. See Weapons for details on weapon types and combinations. Blueprint Tips At any time, you can save your current ship as a blueprint : - Open the Catalog ( U , or the Catalog tab in inventory) - Click Create New Entry - The blueprint is saved and can later be spawned at any shop, provided you supply the required blocks See Catalog & Blueprints for the full catalog guide. Good Building Practices Build symmetrically — a balanced ship handles more predictably. Use symmetry planes (see Advanced Building ) to mirror blocks automatically. Protect your core — the ship core is its most critical block. Surround it with hull and armour. Protect computers and reactors — a destroyed weapon computer disables that weapon system; a destroyed reactor drops available power. Use build mode fast movement ( Left Shift ) to move quickly around large ships.

docs.text: Ship Systems StarMade uses a block-group system to determine how sets of same-type blocks behave together. This is most important for weapons, where grouping affects how shots are fired. What is a Block Group? A block group is a set of blocks of the same type that are all touching each other (face-to-face, not diagonal). A solid cube is one block group. A straight line is also one block group. A single isolated block is its own group. Reactors Reactors are the core of your ship, generating the energy that all other ship systems use to function, and are the central linking point for your reactor chambers , which modify other ship systems. See Reactors . Chambers Chambers are sub-systems that branch off from your reactor and modify the function of other systems on your ship (such as shields, jump drives, and thrusters), or give you new systems (such as scanners and stealth drives). See Chambers . Thrusters Thruster modules add to your ship's maximum speed and acceleration. More blocks equals more thrust. Higher thrust to mass ratio gives you a higher top speed. See Thrusters . Shields Shield modules generate a shield that absorbs damage before it reaches your hull. Shield recharge requires power, so size your reactors to support your shield blocks. See Shields . Weapon and Salvager Groups Each contiguous group of weapon, salvager, or astrotech barrel/module blocks fires as a single shot . You can choose between: Layout Effect All barrels in one touching group One powerful shot Multiple separate groups Multiple weaker simultaneous shots The weapon or salvage computer is a separate block and doesn't need to touch the barrels — it is connected via the link system. See Weapons and Salvagers .

docs.text: Reactors and Stabilizers Every ship needs a power reactor to run its systems. This guide covers how to build and balance your reactor. Core Blocks Block Role Reactor Power Generates power. More blocks = more power regen and a higher reactor level. Reactor Stabilizer Keeps the reactor stable. Below 100% stability the ship takes extra damage. Reactor Conduit Connects chambers to the reactor (see Chambers ). Building a Reactor Reactor Power blocks that touch each other form one reactor. Its power regen increases with every block in it. { "height": 260, "blocks": [ { "from": [0,0,0], "to": [2,2,2], "block": "REACTOR_POWER" } ], "steps": [ { "text": "27 Reactor Power blocks touching each other form one reactor.", "blocks": [] }, { "text": "The first 10 reactor blocks are free; every block after that needs one stabilizer. 27 - 10 = 17 stabilizers for 100% stability.", "blocks": [ { "from": [6,0,0], "to": [6,2,2], "block": "REACTOR_STABILIZER" }, { "from": [-4,0,0], "to": [-4,2,2], "block": "REACTOR_STABILIZER" } ] }, { "text": "Conduits lead from the reactor to its chambers, which unlock extra ship abilities.", "blocks": [ { "from": [1,3,1], "to": [1,4,1], "block": "REACTOR_CONDUIT", "orient": 2 }, { "from": [0,5,0], "to": [2,5,2], "block": "MOBILITY_CHAMBER" } ] } ] } A ship can hold more than one reactor, but only one is active at a time. You can switch the active reactor from the reactor panel; switching has a 10 second cooldown. Stability Stability compares your stabilizers to the size of your active reactor: stability = (10 + stabilizers) ÷ reactor blocks , capped at 100% The first 10 reactor blocks are stabilized for free. After that, you need one stabilizer per reactor block . Stabilizers can go anywhere on the ship — distance and direction from the reactor don't matter. Only your 20 largest stabilizer groups count, so don't scatter them as single blocks all over the hull. Stability does not reduce your power output, but below 100% your ship takes extra damage from beams and explosions (missiles and explosive effects). Cannon hits are not affected. Stability Damage taken 100% Normal 90% About 3× 50% About 11× 0% 21× Tip: Always aim for 100% stability. You can check it in the ship's reactor panel. Losing stabilizers in combat lowers it, so a few spare stabilizers buy you margin. Reactor Level Reactor level goes up by one for every 150 reactor blocks (0–149 blocks is level 0, 150 is level 1, 300 is level 2, and so on). docs.text: Reactor Chambers Chambers are special blocks that plug into your reactor to give your ship additional capabilities — jump drives, stealth, enhanced mobility, and more. They are the primary way to unlock advanced ship systems. How Chambers Work Chambers must be physically connected to the reactor using Reactor Conduit blocks. docs.text: Thrusters Thrusters are modules that allow you to move your ship while consuming energy. Thrusters have a linear power consumption per module, but diminishing returns on how much thrust each thruster module on a ship produces. Larger ships will require more thrusters and more power to move at the same speed as a smaller ship. Thrust to Mass Ratio A ship's thrust to mass ratio (TMR) determines its maximum speed, as well as how fast it can accelerate. The maximum TMR for top speed is 5.0. Thruster Management Menu Opening the radial menu to Ship -> Thrusters opens the Thruster Management menu. In this menu, you can assign the percentage of thrust that goes to each axis of travel, as well as rotational thrust and repulsors. You can also enable "Inherit Thrusters From Docks" to add thrust from docked ships to the main ship, and enable or disable automatic dampeners (passive braking). Repulsors Repulsors use thrust to allow a ship to automatically hover off the ground inside of a gravity field. Enhancing Thrusters With Chambers Chambers can increase your ship's max speed or unlock a "Thrust Blast" system for sudden bursts of acceleration. See the Chambers guide for more details.

docs.text: Shields Shields are your ship's first layer of defence. All incoming damage hits shields before reaching your hull and blocks. When shields are depleted they enter a Shield Outage before recharging. <svg width="640" height="262" viewBox="0 0 640 262" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="sans-serif"> <rect x="1" y="1" width="638" height="260" rx="12" fill="#121821" stroke="#2c3b50" stroke-width="2"/> <text x="320" y="36" text-anchor="middle" fill="#e8eef7" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">Damage Hits Shields First</text> <line x1="36" y1="140" x2="214" y2="140" stroke="#e09a3e" stroke-width="6"/> <polygon points="214,128 240,140 214,152" fill="#e09a3e"/> <text x="42" y="124" fill="#e09a3e" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Incoming damage</text> <rect x="250" y="64" width="350" height="152" rx="14" fill="#10303b" stroke="#4fc3e8" stroke-width="2"/> <rect x="296" y="92" width="258" height="96" rx="10" fill="#2a313b" stroke="#c3ccd8" stroke-width="2"/> <rect x="348" y="116" width="154" height="48" rx="8" fill="#1b232f" stroke="#8e9bac" stroke-width="2"/> <rect x="408" y="128" width="34" height="24" rx="4" fill="#4a3a1a" stroke="#e0b057"/> <text x="270" y="84" fill="#7fdcf2" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">SHIELDS</text> <text x="312" y="110" fill="#dde3ec" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">ARMOR</text> <text x="425" y="186" text-anchor="middle" fill="#aab7c6" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">SYSTEMS</text> <text x="320" y="246" text-anchor="middle" fill="#8e9bac" font-size="13">When shields are depleted they enter an outage; hits then pass to armor, then internal systems.</text> </svg> Shield Capacitor Blocks Place Shield Capacitor blocks on your ship to add shield capacity. Each block contributes: Stat Value per block Capacity 250 Every contiguous group of Shield Capacitors forms a Capacity Bank. A ship can only have up to 20 Capacity Banks , so make sure your Shield Capacitors are grouped together to avoid going over the limit. Shield Recharger Blocks and Shield Radius Shield Rechargers convert Reactor Power into Shields, which are stored by Shield Capacitors inside their Shield Radius . Each block contributes: Stat Value per block Recharge 5/second And costs: Stat Value per block Reactor Power 10/second This Reactor Power cost does not change whether the Shield Rechargers are resting or actively charging. Shield Radius (the zone around your ship that the shield covers) projects from the center of each contiguous group of Shield Rechargers , and scales up with block count on an exponential curve — small ships get good coverage quickly; large ships need proportionally more blocks for full hull coverage. It is not a "shield bubble"; The shield is skin-tight to the hull of the ship, and the Shield Radius just shows what part of the hull is covered. Each contiguous group of Shield Rechargers produces its own Shield Radius . If the center of one Shield Radius is inside another Shield Radius , the smaller of the two will be disabled. Shield Radius determines which which Capacity Banks are charged by which Shield Recharger group. To be charged, a Capacity Bank must be inside the Shield Recharger group's Shield Radius . Each Capacity Bank can only belong to one Shield Recharger group, so in the event of Shield Radius overlap, the Capacity Bank will go to the largest Shield Recharger group. Capacity Bank ownership is indicated by pink arrows from the center of the Capacity Bank to the center of the Shield Recharger group. Shield Upkeep Each point of Shield Capacity also requires 0.004 points of Shield Upkeep per second. This equates to 1 point per block of Shield Capacitors . If Shield Recharge is less than the Shield Upkeep cost, the Capacity Bank will drain until it reaches zero. Recharge Behaviour A Shield Recharger group that has not taken any damage for the last 30 seconds will recharge at its full rate regardless of how much Shield Capacity the group currently has. Shield Under Fire is a debuff that lasts for 30 seconds after a Shield Recharger group has taken Shield damage. During this time, Shield Recharge is reduced, from a 0% reduction at 100% Shield Capacity to a 50% reduction at 20% Shield Capacity . The amount of reduction is based on the lowest percentage the Shield Recharger group reached while afflicted with the debuff, rather than the current Shield Capacity . Shield Outage is a debuff that lasts for 10 seconds after a Shield Recharger group has reached 0% Shield Capacity . During this time, Shield Recharge for this group is completely disabled. Turrets/Docks Shield Interaction Turrets and docked ships have their shields disabled while they are docked. When they are hit by weapons, they will be protected by the shields of the ship or station they are docked to instead. Improving Shields with Chambers Shield-related chamber trees can boost: - Total capacity (more buffer before breaking) - Shield upkeep (less shield upkeep cost) - Recovery time (shorter lockout after shield break) See the Chambers guide for details. Tips and Tricks While it is possible to have multiple groups of Shield Rechargers on one ship, it is almost always better to just have a single group that covers the entire ship. It's important to make sure you have enough Shield Regen to still regenerate while afflicted with the Shield Under Fire debuff. If your Shield Upkeep exceeds your Shield Regen you will rapidly lose your shields and start taking hull damage.

docs.text: Weapons StarMade has three primary weapon types, three utility weapons, and explosive warhead blocks. Primary weapons can be linked to a secondary weapon to alter the functions and stats of the primary weapon, and can be linked to an effect system to alter its damage type distribution. Some weapons require weapon capacity to fire. Weapon Types Primary Weapons : Weapon Primary Role Secondary Role Cannon Simple direct-fire projectile Shorter range, higher rate of fire Missile Complex explosive projectile Higher damage, charge up time Damage Beam Hitscan damage beam Longer range, slower rate of fire Utility Weapons (no direct damage): Weapon Role Push Pulse Knocks back nearby ships; deals no direct damage Tractor Beam Pulls, pushes, or tows ships and loose objects Astrotech Beam Repairs damaged or destroyed blocks on ships Block Weapons (deal damage on block contact): Weapon Role Warhead Explodes on contact with another ship; ignores shields Setting Up a Weapon Every weapon system consists of two block types: Weapon Computer — the controller. Assign it to a hotbar slot. One per weapon system. Weapon Modules — the actual firepower. More modules = more damage. Steps Place a Weapon Computer on your ship in build mode. Place Weapon Modules anywhere on the ship (they don't need to touch the computer). Open the Weapon Panel ( G ). Drag the computer into a hotbar slot. Close the panel, switch to flight mode, and select the weapon slot. Weapon Computer Module Cannon Cannon Computer Cannon Barrel Missile Missile Computer Missile Tube Beam Damage Beam Computer Damage Beam Module Push Pulse Push Pulse Computer Push Pulse Module Tractor Beam Tractor Beam Computer Tractor Beam Module Combination System By linking a Secondary Weapon computer and modules to a Primary Weapon , you can alter the function of the primary weapon, like its range, reload speed, and damage. Including the 3 basic primary weapons, there are 12 total Weapon Combinations , each with unique stats and function. The ratio of weapon modules linked to the Secondary Weapon compared to the Primary Weapon determines how much of the modification effect is applied, with 100% of the effect being applied at a 1:1 ratio. Experiment with partial secondary effects to find the perfect weapon for your niche! A weapon computer can only be used in one combination at a time . Primary Weapon Cannon Secondary Damage Beam Secondary Missile Secondary No Secondary Cannon Machine Gun Sniper Cannon Charge Cannon Basic Cannon Damage Beam Constant Beam Sniper Beam Charge Beam Burst Beam Missile Heat-Seeking Swarms Long Range Lock On Inertia Bomb Dumbfire Missile Missile/Missile creates a special shield-ignoring bomb that has no velocity of its own and must be launched from a fast moving ship. Effect System Connecting certain effect systems to a weapon computer changes the damage type distribution (Kinetic, Heat, EM). This will make a weapon stronger against one type of defenses and weaker against the others. At a 1:1 Primary Weapon to Effect System ratio, the damage will be increased by 33.3% for the specified damage type and reduced by 16.6% for the other two types. A primary weapon can be linked to both a secondary weapon and an effect system at the same time. Each weapon type has a different default damage distribution , making them better suited for dealing with different types of targets. Weapon Type Kinetic Heat EM Cannons 50% 16.6% 33.3% Damage Beams 16.6% 33.3% 50% Missiles 16.6% 50% 33.3% See the Armor & Damage guide for how damage types interact with shields and armor. Linking via the Weapon Panel Open the Weapon Panel ( G ). Find your primary weapon computer in the list. Drag the secondary weapon computer into the secondary slot of the primary. The coloured borders on the computers in the world indicate the connection. To unlink, drag the secondary out of its slot and drop it in the unlink box . You can also link and unlink in-world: press C on the primary computer, then V on the secondary computer. Weapon Capacity Missiles require Missile Capacity to fire. Missile Capacity Modules give a ship Missile Capacity , which is consumed when firing a missile . If a ship's Missile Capacity is not full, it will start reloading, with the length of time depending on how much Missile Capacity the ship has. Each Missile Capacity Module added gives diminishing returns, with the first few blocks giving a lot of Missile Capacity , but further capacity requiring exponentially more modules for each additional unit. This creates a soft cap on the number of missiles that a single ship can actually fire in a single volley. Projectile Colour Link a Light Source block to a weapon computer (using C to select, then V to connect) to change the colour of that weapon's projectiles to match the light colour. Utility Weapons Utility weapons do no damage on their own, instead having some sort of support function to either reduce the effectiveness of an enemy or boost the effectiveness of your own ships. Push Pulse Push Pulse projects an area of effect pulse that pushes ships away from its origin point. The more modules, the larger and more powerful the pushing effect is. Tractor Beam Tractor Beams can push, pull, and stop a ship or asteroid by applying force at the point of the beam's impact. More modules increases the tractor strength. A small, slowly drifting asteroid is much easier to stop than a large ship that is actively fighting the tractor beam with its own thrusters. The ship must not have been edited with build mode after the blocks were destroyed for it to be repaired by an astrotech beam, as astrotech restores the ship to its last saved state. More modules increases the amount of blocks restored with each burst of the beam. There is a cooldown period after taking block damage before any blocks can be repaired by an astrotech beam. All warheads in a contiguous group are automatically linked together and will detonate together, with the strength of the explosion determined by how many blocks are in the group. The explosion from warheads ignores shields. Warheads can be combined with shootout rails and a Bobby AI module to create powerful, single use "torpedo" ships that attempt to ram enemy ships with their warheads.

docs.text: Missiles require Missile Capacity to fire. Missile Capacity Modules give a ship Missile Capacity , which is consumed when firing a missile . Each Missile Capacity Module added gives diminishing returns, with the first few blocks giving a lot of Missile Capacity , but further capacity requiring exponentially more modules for each additional unit. This creates a soft cap on the number of missiles that a single ship can actually fire in a single volley.

Armor thickness is only calculated up to 32 blocks, but thicker armor is still more durable as it can maintain a 32 block thickness even as outer layers of the hull are destroyed. Overpenetration occurs when a cannon hit does more than 20 times an armor block's HP before accounting for reduction by armor value. When overpenetrating , the cannon shell will pass straight through the block instead of stopping and spreading damage to all surrounding blocks. Overpenetration does not apply to damage beams and missiles. Key Takeaways and Practical Implications Small hits are almost completely absorbed. A wall of armor is nearly impenetrable against many weak shots. Massive single cannon hits penetrate. A cannon shot doing more than 20× the armor block's HP bypasses it entirely via overpenetration . docs.text: Ship & Turret AI A ship, station turret or docked entity with a BOBBY AI Module can fly and fight on its own. Only one AI Module is allowed per ship. Setting Up AI Place a BOBBY AI Module on the ship. Press R on it to open the AI panel. You can also press ; (or the AI button on the top bar) while you are in the ship. Pick a Type and tick Active . Entering a ship's core or a cockpit turns its AI off. Turn it back on when you leave. The AI also switches off if the ship's core overheats. A logic signal into the AI Module turns the AI on or off. Types Type What it does Ship Hunts enemies within 3 sectors, flies to them and fights Turret Stays docked, turns to face targets in weapon range and fires Fleet Waits for orders from its fleet. See Fleets The game picks some of these for you: An entity docked on the last axis of a turret becomes a Turret . See Docking & Turrets . A ship that joins a fleet becomes Fleet and turns on; when it leaves the fleet it goes back to Ship . Who the AI Attacks The AI attacks whoever its faction is at war with. Pirates are enemies of everyone. A ship without a faction only fights Pirates (and other factions that attack neutrals). Docked turrets without their own faction use the host's faction. The AI never targets shops, cloaked ships, or anything in a protected sector. When a Ship AI is hit by an enemy, it turns on the attacker (at most once every 25 seconds). The AI Panel General Setting What it does Active Turns the AI on or off Type Ship, Turret or Fleet Remote Control Turrets only: lets the host's pilot aim the turrets (see below) Priority How to choose between targets: Random, Closest, Furthest, Weakest, Strongest, Lightest, Heaviest, Lowest shields, Highest shields Keep target until lost Stay on one target instead of picking again every scan Minimum range Ship AI: the distance to keep from its target. Auto fights up close Maximum range Ship AI: how far away it fights from. It can't be more than the range of your weapons. Auto uses your weapon range Multi-Output Fire Mode Volley makes every cannon and missile fire in volleys; Simultaneous leaves each weapon's own setting Missile Damage Prioritization Shown when Missiles is first in Aim At: shoot the missiles with the Highest or Lowest damage first, or Random Aim At An ordered list of what turrets shoot at: Selected Target , Ships , Stations , Missiles , Astronauts and Asteroids . Turn each one on or off and move it up or down; the turret goes for the first kind it finds. New AIs aim at Ships, Stations and Astronauts. Selected Target: the target the host's pilot has pinned for the AI ( X while flying), or the host AI's own target. Missiles: point defence. Turrets shoot down enemy missiles in range. Asteroids: a turret with salvage beams mines nearby asteroids. Focus Fire Pick which systems the AI shoots at on its target, in priority order: Reactors, Stabilizers, Chambers, Thrusters, Shield Rechargers, Shield Capacitors. With focus fire off, the AI aims at a random system on the target. How Ship AI Fights It flies to the target and stops a bit inside its weapon range (or at its Minimum range), then circles while firing. Against targets on a planet it makes strafing runs instead: dive, fire, pull up and turn back for another pass. A ship armed with only warheads rams its target. It steers around other ships and gas giants in its way. When it loses its target it stays where it is and searches again every few seconds. It doesn't flee, patrol or go home. Out of combat it uses its scanner; in combat it uses cloaking, jamming and jump inhibitors if it has them. With no thrusters it barely moves. How Turrets Fight Turrets only look for targets within their weapon range . The range sliders don't affect them. Turrets lead moving targets (except beam-only turrets). docs.text: Navigation The StarMade universe is vast. Understanding its structure and using the navigation tools efficiently will save you a lot of time. Universe Structure The universe is organised into sectors grouped into systems . Sectors A sector is the basic unit of space. Your current sector coordinates ( [X, Y, Z] ) are always displayed at the top of your HUD next to your player name. Each sector can contain: Planets and their surrounding space Asteroid fields Trading stations and NPC structures Other players' ships and bases Empty space Systems A system is a 16 × 16 × 16 cube of sectors. A star is usually located near the centre of each system. Resources and encounter types vary depending on how far a sector is from the star. Distance from the star affects asteroid types. Rare mineral asteroids are more likely to appear in sectors farther from the star. The Navigation Panel Press N to open the Navigation Panel. It lists every object in your current and adjacent sectors. Filters Use the filter checkboxes to show or hide: - Planets - Asteroids - Stations - Ships (player and NPC) - Jump beacons - Debris Selecting a Target Click any entry in the navigation list to select it. A selection indicator appears on your HUD pointing toward the selected object, making it easy to fly to it without having to spot it visually. Waypoints To navigate to a specific sector coordinate: Open the Navigation Panel ( N ). Click the Waypoint button. Enter the [X, Y, Z] coordinates of your destination sector. A white blinking arrow appears on your HUD pointing toward the waypoint. Waypoints persist until you remove them. You can use them to mark resource-rich sectors, player bases, or planned routes. Practical Tips Your starting sector usually contains a Trading Guild station — check the navigation panel immediately to locate it. Asteroid field sectors are clearly visible in space; approach any dark-coloured irregular objects. When travelling long distances, set a waypoint and use full thrust ( W held). Ships have a natural speed cap per sector, but there is no global travel limit. You can select an entity in the world directly by looking at it and pressing F — this selects it in the HUD without opening the nav panel.

docs.text: Resources & Mining Raw resources are the foundation of everything you build. There are two families of raw materials, each found in different places across the universe. Resource Types Type Appearance Found On Ores Coloured rock chunks Asteroids, planet surfaces Crystal Shards Glowing crystalline Asteroids, planet surfaces Each ore and shard type has a different colour and name (e.g. Threns Ore, Hattel Shards). For basic crafting the specific type matters less than whether it is an ore or a shard — you just need enough of either to start. Where to Find Resources Asteroids Asteroid fields appear as clusters of grey-brown irregular objects in space. Each asteroid type always contains the same mineral type — once you know what a particular asteroid looks like, you know what it will drop. Planets Planet surfaces contain ore and shard deposits, but they are more sparsely distributed than asteroids. Each planet face has two random resource types which are set when the planet generates. Planets are large — flying across the surface to locate veins takes time, but they can yield large quantities in one location once found. How to Mine As an Astronaut Hold the right mouse button while looking at a resource block. Your character fires a mining beam. The block breaks after a short duration and drops items into your inventory automatically. Make sure no weapon is selected (scroll past the last weapon slot or press the mouse wheel to deselect). With a Ship Build a Salvage Computer and Salvage Beam Modules on your ship (same setup as weapons). Aim the salvage beam at asteroid or planet blocks to harvest them rapidly. Ships can mine much faster than astronaut mode and collect materials directly into the ship's storage. Processing Raw Materials Raw ores and shards cannot be used directly — they must be processed into capsules first, then into crafting ingredients. See Crafting Basics for the full processing chain. Quick Resource Reference Ingredient Source Ore capsule Process ore in personal capsule refinery or factory Shard capsule Process crystal shards in personal capsule refinery or factory Metal Mesh 10 ore capsules in personal micro-factory or factory Crystal Circuit 10 shard capsules in personal micro-factory or factory Both Metal Mesh and Crystal Circuit are the base ingredients for nearly every craftable block in the game.

docs.text: Asteroids Asteroids are highly concentrated deposits of Raw Materials found in space orbiting stars. They are harvested with ship-based Salvage Systems. Types Asteroids are a vital part of mining, and resource acquisition in Starmade. There are eight types of asteroids, each with different mineral, crystal, and ore composition. They are located in asteroid orbital sectors in solar systems. Orbital sectors will have multiple asteroids at the center of them. If all the asteroids are destroyed, new ones will be generated eventually on a sector reload. It should be noted that as of StarMade v0.198.219, Yellow "Lukrah" asteroids are now similar in colour to Red "Cinnabar" Asteroids at a glance. It is recommended you activate Asteroid navigation markers and use that to aid in finding and differentiating them. Without using Asteroid navigation markers, one noticeable difference between the two is that the Yellow "Lukrah" asteroids are a solid dark red, while the Red "Cinnabar" Asteroids are a mix of dark red with a lighter shade of red spots covering it. Sandy ( Orange ) Chabaz Parseen Sapsun Outer belts Also contains Ice. Sandy ( Red with spots ) Cinnabar Varat Zercaner Middle and outer belts Also contains Lava. Spawning Asteroids spawn throughout star-systems in a very predictable, and structured manner, making it easy to find resources. Player Interaction Asteroids cannot be inhabited like planets or stations, but Faction Modules may be placed on them and the asteroid can then become associated with a faction. This can allow players to make a weapon entity that is mobile through the use of Pull/Push effects or a Push-Pulse System and appears neutral, but houses weapons or turrets. While they cannot be truly inhabited, Blocks such as Build Blocks, Factories, and Undeathinators still function on them, serving as a replacement temporary base to using a Planet. However, the system cannot be claimed from an Asteroid nor can it be made a Homebase. docs.text: Crafting Basics StarMade's crafting system is based on a consistence tree — a hierarchy of ingredients where higher-tier items are made from lower-tier ones, all the way down to raw ores and shards. The Consistence Tree Think of crafting like a tree with branches: The root is the item you want to make. Each branch is an ingredient required for that item. Each ingredient branch has its own sub-branches (its own ingredients). Trees never loop — an item is never an ingredient of itself. A factory only performs the last step of a tree. To make a Power Reactor Module, the factory consumes Metal Mesh and Active Varat Processor — you need a separate factory to make each of those from their own ingredients. Recipes (Fixed) Some items use a recipe instead of a consistence tree. These are fixed: Recipe Output 10 ore capsules (any type) 1 Metal Mesh 10 shard capsules (any type) 1 Crystal Circuit Step-by-Step: First Materials 1. Mine Raw Resources Go to an asteroid field and mine ores and shards with the right mouse button (no weapon selected). 2. Personal Capsule Refinery Open your inventory ( I ) and click Craft Capsule . This opens your personal capsule refinery. Put one stack of raw ore or shards in the input slot. Leave the second slot empty — the product (capsules) will appear there. Wait for processing to complete. You can only process one type at a time in the personal refinery because it needs a free slot for the output. Factory blocks are more efficient for bulk processing. 3. Personal Micro-Factory In your inventory, click Micro to open the personal micro-factory. Place 10 capsules (all the same type: all ore capsules, or all shard capsules). After a moment you get: 10 ore capsules → 1 Metal Mesh 10 shard capsules → 1 Crystal Circuit 4. Personal Macro-Factory Craft When you have 10 Metal Meshes or 10 Crystal Circuits , click Craft Macro in your inventory to craft your first Macro Factory block. This factory can produce any craftable block in the game — see Factories & Production for how to use it. Material Summary Raw → Capsule Capsule × 10 → Ore → Ore Capsule Metal Mesh Shard → Shard Capsule Crystal Circuit Metal Mesh and Crystal Circuit are ingredients in virtually every block recipe.
